title.en: Sacred treasure of the Taiping kingdom

alt.en: The reverse of a square-holed coin bears the two characters sheng bao, “sacred treasure”; museum label, scale, colour chart and watermark remain visible.
alt.zh: 方孔钱背面铸“圣宝”二字；来源照片的藏品标签、标尺、色卡与水印均予保留。

caption.en: Reverse of a Taiping Tianguo coin, National Museum of History 78-01051. The obverse names the kingdom; the reverse calls its money “sacred treasure”. The exact mint and casting year are not recorded.
caption.zh: 国立历史博物馆78-01051号太平天国钱背面。正面列国号，背面称“圣宝”；具体铸地与铸造年份未载。

interpretation.en: Hong Xiuquan’s kingdom joined religious authority to government. The words “sacred treasure” put that claim onto money, complementing the religious publications discussed in his biography.
interpretation.zh: 洪秀全的政权将宗教权威与统治相结合。“圣宝”二字把这种宣示带到钱币上，与传记所述宗教出版物相互参照。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Taiping period, 1851–1864; exact casting year unrecorded

title.en: Li Zicheng’s reign name on money
title.zh: 钱币上的李自成永昌年号

alt.en: A corroded round coin with a square hole and four raised characters, Yongchang tongbao; the museum label and colour scale remain below.
alt.zh: 圆形锈蚀钱币中央有方孔，四周铸“永昌通宝”；下方保留馆藏标签与色标。

caption.en: Yongchang tongbao, a five-cash denomination of Li Zicheng’s Shun regime, catalogued to 1644–1645. This example entered the National Museum of History in 1988.
caption.zh: 李自成大顺政权的永昌通宝折五钱，馆藏说明列铸行期为1644—1645年；本件1988年入藏国立历史博物馆。

interpretation.en: A new reign name made the claim to rule visible in an everyday object. The coin accompanies Li’s move from rebellion to state-building, while its five-cash denomination points to administration as well as conquest. Its findspot and individual mint are not recorded.
interpretation.zh: 新年号把统治主张铸进日常物件。此钱对应李自成由反叛走向建政的过程，折五面值也提示征服之外的行政需求；本件出土地与具体铸局未载。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Yongchang era, 1644–1645; individual casting year unrecorded

title.en: Han Lin’er’s Longfeng reign on a coin
title.zh: 钱币上的韩林儿龙凤年号

alt.en: A green-patinated square-holed coin reads Longfeng tongbao, with the museum number, scale, colour chart and watermark retained.
alt.zh: 带绿色锈层的方孔钱铸“龙凤通宝”，并保留馆藏编号、标尺、色卡与水印。

caption.en: Longfeng tongbao of Han Lin’er’s late-Yuan Song regime. The museum connects this coin type with Liu Futong’s enthronement of Han at Bozhou in 1355; this example’s exact casting year is not given.
caption.zh: 元末韩林儿宋政权的龙凤通宝。馆藏说明将这一钱种与1355年刘福通拥韩林儿于亳州称帝相连；本件具体铸年未载。

interpretation.en: The new regime asserted authority through its own calendar and coinage. The characters above and below the square hole name the Longfeng era; those at right and left read tongbao, “circulating treasure”.
interpretation.zh: 新政权通过自立年号与铸币宣示权威。方孔上下的文字组成“龙凤”年号，右左两字为“通宝”。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Longfeng era of Han Lin’er; after its inauguration in 1355; exact year unrecorded

title.en: The Yongli court’s name survives on money
title.zh: 钱币保存的永历朝廷年号

alt.en: A mottled green-brown coin with a square hole bears Yongli tongbao; the photograph retains accession label, colour chart, scale and watermark.
alt.zh: 绿褐相间的方孔钱铸“永历通宝”；照片保留馆藏标签、色卡、标尺与水印。

caption.en: Yongli tongbao with gong on the reverse, catalogued to the Yongli coinage of 1647–1662. Zhu Youlang was enthroned at Zhaoqing in 1646 and named the following year Yongli 1.
caption.zh: 背面有“工”字的永历通宝，馆藏说明列铸行期为1647—1662年。朱由榔1646年在肇庆即位，以次年为永历元年。

interpretation.en: A reign name on money carried the Southern Ming court’s claim beyond a palace proclamation. This coin illustrates the political authority associated with Yongli, rather than the accession ceremony itself. Its precise mint and findspot are not established in this catalog.
interpretation.zh: 钱币上的年号，把南明朝廷的政治主张带出宫廷宣告的场合。本件表现与永历相连的统治权威，而非即位仪式本身；馆藏记录未确定其具体铸局与出土地。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Yongli coinage, 1647–1662; exact casting year unrecorded
